title: Beer Made from Leftover Rice Proves Popular in Japan
paragraphs: A craft beer made from rice that's left over from rice cooker testing has proven popular in Japan.
The company behind the beer, kitchen appliance maker Zojirushi, says it has met its goal of selling 100,000 cans of its "Zo-no-mai" beer in just six months.
When developing new rice cookers, Zojirushi staff have to cook and taste test rice repeatedly. As a result, there's always a lot of rice left over, most of which gets composted.
But in 2023, the company released its first craft beer made from leftover rice, a lager called "Hare to ho."
That beer was made with the help of Isekado Brewery, a company based in Mie prefecture.

Zojirushi released its second beer in March this year, a golden ale called "Zo-no-mai," which means "Elephant Dance." The name comes partly from the company logo — which is an elephant — and the company name, Zojirushi, which means "elephant mark" in Japanese.
The company says the beer smells like citrus and has a light and refreshing taste that pairs well with Japanese food.
In fact, it says the new beer is tasty enough to make an elephant get up and dance! But the name is also a play on words because the characters for "dance" and "rice" can both be pronounced as "mai."
Zojirushi worked with Niigata prefecture's Echigo Beer, Japan's first craft beer brewery, to create the beer.
Zojirushi says it creates about 30 metric tons of food waste a year, and just 5% of this can be used to make beer. However, the company says it's looking for more ways to upcycle its leftover rice.
